chogan595.comparison: Same file and function (move() in www/games/snakes/index.html) and the same change as PR #599: stop calling next() synchronously, schedule it with later(next, anim.pts[0].ms), and add C.feedback('place') for the first square. Only placement of the feedback call differs (before render vs after).
chogan595.what_went_wrong: Nothing in the pipeline. The project's own test command did not finish inside the 4-minute cap in the sandbox, before or after the patch (stopped in the Gorillas section; the Snakes and Ladders section had passed both times), so 'own tests still pass' is unproven. The two 4-minute test runs are why the fix step took 11 minutes.

chogan506.comparison: Same line and same logic as PR #509 for the eightball page (drop Math.abs so a leftward drag clamps to 0). The maintainers moved the formula into Cue.barPower() in www/lib/cue.js and applied it to BOTH eightball and snooker; the agent patched only eightball, so the identical bug remains in www/games/snooker/index.html.
chogan506.what_went_wrong: Fix is correct for the page in the report but incomplete: the same line in the snooker page was not touched. The pipeline's own check cannot see that, because the reproduction only exercises eightball. Own tests timed out at the 4-minute cap before and after (the agent also noted 1 vs 2 CPU-timing assertion failures in unrelated sections, which looks like sandbox timing noise).

drawdb858.comparison: No fix produced. Maintainers' fix (PR #943) holds the width in temporary modal state and commits on Confirm.
drawdb858.what_went_wrong: Timeout in the reproduce step (720 s limit). Install and dev server were fine. The watcher's report was accurate, but the recording starts mid-session on a diagram with tables (the University template). A fresh local app first shows a 'Pick a database' modal and has an empty canvas, and the agent spent the whole budget trying to drive the semi-ui modals and menus to get tables on screen. Every command also restarted the dev server because background processes do not survive between tool calls. A second pass with an 18-minute reproduce limit (same report, fresh sandbox) also timed out at the same place, and hit a sandbox snapshot-upload error along the way, so this is not just a tight clock.
drawdb858.extended_review: Still a timeout with an 18-minute reproduce limit (1086 s, 675k tokens). Same obstacle: getting past the 'Pick a database' modal and putting tables on the canvas. One command also failed on a sandbox snapshot-upload error.

wavesurfer3742.comparison: No fix attempted. Maintainers' fix (PR #3743) is one line in initTimeline(): take pxPerSec from the waveform wrapper's scrollWidth when the timeline lives in its own container.
wavesurfer3742.what_went_wrong: Not reproduced (BUG_ABSENT 3/3), and that verdict is true for what was tested. The bug only happens when the timeline is given its own `container`. The issue title says so ('if not contained in Wavesurfer wrapper'), but the watcher's report dropped that condition and described only 'timeline does not rescale on zoom'. The stock timeline example at this commit renders the timeline inside the waveform, where it works. The video cannot show which option the reporter's code used; the snippet is in the issue body, which the pipeline was deliberately not given.

wavesurfer2963.comparison: No fix attempted. Maintainers' fix (PR #2984) is 3 lines in src/draggable.ts: ignore pointerdown from the right mouse button.
wavesurfer2963.what_went_wrong: Not reproduced (BUG_ABSENT 3/3) although the bug is in the code at this commit. The watcher's report was right. In a real browser the native context menu swallows the pointerup after a right-click, which leaves the drag handler armed. Playwright's page.mouse.click(button='right') in headless Chrome sends a clean down+up pair and no native menu appears, so the stuck state never occurs. The agent followed the steps literally and did not think to send a right-button pointerdown with no matching pointerup. A false negative caused by browser-automation fidelity.

panels650.comparison: No fix produced. Maintainers' fix (PR #651) comments out the collapsible-panel branch added in #635 and skips 5 of the project's own unit tests.
panels650.what_went_wrong: Timeout in the reproduce step (720 s limit). The watcher took 187 s and wrote a precise report (which docs example, drag distances, the 100 px to 200 px jump). pnpm install and the Vite docs site started fine. The agent then lost its time finding and navigating to the 'Collapsible panels' example (the nav links are not anchors) and restarting the dev server for every attempt.
panels650.extended_review: With the longer limit it reproduced in 751 s (31 s past the first-pass limit) and then fixed in 551 s. Fix is in the same file and function as PR #651 (adjustLayoutByDelta.ts, the collapsible branch added in #635) but a different approach: the maintainers commented the whole branch out and skipped 5 of their own tests; the agent kept the branch and only runs it when the panel starts collapsed. The project's own suite passed before and after (29 files, 382 tests), including the 5 tests the maintainers had to skip. Plausible and arguably less destructive, but the reproduction checks only the first of the two examples in the recording (the jump from minSize), not the collapsedSize example, so the second symptom is unverified.

wavesurfer3494.comparison: Same file (src/plugins/regions.ts), same three places, same mechanism as PR #3496: pass the resized side through the region 'update' event (the type change and emit('update', side) lines are identical). Maintainers then skip adjustScroll() entirely while resizing; the agent keeps auto-scroll for the edge being dragged and suppresses only the opposite edge, plus an extra guard for regions wider than the viewport when dragging. Slightly larger than the maintainers' patch but arguably keeps more behaviour.
wavesurfer3494.what_went_wrong: Nothing material. The reproduction asserts on the scroll position jumping to 0 during and after the drag (one part of the reported symptom), not on the blank/smeared rendering. No project tests were run (Cypress only).

drawdb687.comparison: No fix produced. Maintainers' fix (PR #692): only call setSearchParams when a shareId is present, and use replace:true, so opening /editor does not push an extra history entry.
drawdb687.what_went_wrong: Timeout in the reproduce step (720 s limit). The recording shows the public site reached from a Google results page, with browser Back/Forward. The watcher transcribed the navigation faithfully but its expected/actual centres on 'homepage entry lost after back-forward-forward', one of the variants in the issue. In the sandbox the landing page crashed without its external services (tweet embeds, star counter), and the agent spent its time stubbing those and faking an external 'search' origin.
drawdb687.extended_review: With the longer limit the agent finished in 644 s and reported not_reproduced (BUG_ABSENT 3/3): in headless Chrome, Back from /editor returned to the homepage every time. The issue itself calls the behaviour inconsistent; the script followed the watcher's back-back-forward-forward variant and never asserted on the extra history entry that the maintainers' fix removes.

chogan491.comparison: Same line in ui.fly() in www/lib/chogan.js as PR #497: clamp the start scale k. Maintainers clamp to [0.25, 1.25]; the agent clamps to at most 1 with no lower bound. The maintainers' new regression check (start scale between 1 and 1.25 for a wide seat) would pass with the agent's value of 1.0.
chogan491.what_went_wrong: Nothing in reproduce or fix; the agent chose a phone-sized viewport on its own and caught a one-frame glitch. Own tests timed out at the 4-minute cap before and after. Case used 1150 s of the 1200 s budget.

datepicker5573.comparison: The diff left in the sandbox is equivalent to PR #5584: isSelectedYear() in src/year.tsx returns Boolean(selected && year === getYear(selected)) instead of !selected || ... (maintainers wrote !!selected && ...).
datepicker5573.what_went_wrong: Counted as a timeout: the fix agent was cancelled at the 20-minute case limit before giving its final answer. By then it had patched the file, got BUG_ABSENT 3/3, run the project's jest suite before and after (1022/1022 passed both times, about 2 minutes each) and saved the diff; it was tidying an unrelated package.json reformat that the build had produced. Yarn 4 install plus build plus docs-site install took most of the reproduce step. An earlier attempt at this case is void: the operator config gave no concrete port, the watcher left start_url empty and the gate stopped it as needs_info (a harness mistake, fixed by giving http://localhost:5173/).

recharts6618.comparison: Identical to PR #6623: add key={page} to <CodeEditorWithPreview> in www/src/views/ExamplesView.tsx.
recharts6618.what_went_wrong: Nothing, but slow: the reproduce step took 713 s of its 720 s limit (two npm installs and a library build), so this passed by seconds.

sonner512.comparison: Same handler (Toast onPointerMove in src/index.tsx) and the same two expressions as PR #513, character for character: swipeAmount = y === 'top' ? Math.min(0, yPosition) : Math.max(0, yPosition) and Math.abs(swipeAmount) > 0. The agent also moved the isHighlighted early return above setIsSwiped, which the maintainers did not.
sonner512.what_went_wrong: Nothing in the run. Caveat: the patch matches the upstream line exactly. The trace shows no network lookup (the agent read src/styles.css and edited), and the expression is the obvious one, but sonner is a very popular library, so the model may simply know the later source from training.

_notes: Inputs per case: the reporter's video, the issue title, and operator configuration (repo, pre-fix SHA, install/start command, local URL, test command). The issue body, the fix PR and the fix were never given to the pipeline. The reviewer read them only afterwards, to score.

Limits: 20 minutes per case; inside that, 12 minutes for the reproduce step and the remainder for the fix step. Three cases (drawdb858, panels650, drawdb687) hit the 12-minute reproduce limit. They were re-run once with an 18-minute reproduce limit and a 30-minute case limit, reusing the same watcher report; those results are under extended_pass_not_counted and are NOT in the summary.

Own tests: the fix prompt caps each test run at 4 minutes. chogan's `node tools/test.js` did not finish inside that cap in the sandbox in any of the three chogan cases, so those are 'inconclusive', not 'passing'. Cypress/Playwright e2e suites (wavesurfer.js, sonner) and the large recharts root suite were not run at all.

datepicker5573 was run twice. The first run is void (operator config had no concrete port, so the watcher left start_url empty and the gate returned needs_info); it is kept as data/real_runs/_void_datepicker5573_no_url.json. The counted run used http://localhost:5173/.

Models were left as in the existing pipeline: Neon watches, Hydrogen drives the reproduce agent, Neon drives the fix agent. Nothing was re-run to get a better outcome; every case has exactly one counted run.

'fixed per own script' means the pipeline's own claim (its reproduction printed BUG_ABSENT after the patch). No independent verifier was run on these cases, unlike the planted-bug evaluation. The reviewer checked from the traces that the fix step edited only source files and not the reproduction scripts.

Leak scan: every command and tool call in the agent traces was searched for GitHub issue/PR/commit pages, the GitHub API, gh, extra git fetches, CDN or npm lookups of published versions, and web search. No hits in any counted or extended run. The clone had its remote removed after fetching the single pre-fix commit. This does not rule out the models knowing these public fixes from training (see sonner512).
Not attempted: fortune-sheet #500, excalidraw #8346 and the remaining candidates (time).
